text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- EDF utility chairman Edmond Alphandery says the prices of the state-owned electricity supplier will fall by 14 percent over a four-year period, as agreed with the government.
-- Government to launch early retirement scheme for private-sector doctors from the age of 56.
-- Local tax pressure is increasing, according to report by Credit Local de France.
-- Pilots' SNPL union at Air France Europe against use of strikes without notice to protest conditions of a planned merger with Air France.
-- Cap Gemini posts a 280-million-franc profit for 1996 from 52 million in 1995.
-- Reuters to close down GLOBEX after-hours transactions system in 1998.
-- Households slightly less pessimistic over future economic conditions, INSEE January survey shows.
-- Asset sales accelerate at the Paris bourse since the beginning of the year.
-- Birthrate and marriage rate rose in 1996 from 1995 in France, INSEE says.
